status: approved_for_implementation; per-segment fare and tariff inputs remain scenario-specific
normalization: min-max within the same feasible candidate set for one scenario
hard_constraints: Exclude unreachable, invalid, illegal, or incomplete routes before scoring; weights cannot offset a hard constraint failure.
constant_dimension: A dimension with no variation in the eligible set contributes zero after normalization.

segment_economics.net_economic_cost_formula: sum over journey segments (known operating costs - known fare revenue)
segment_economics.segment_accounting: Retain one ledger row per deadhead or passenger journey segment, with segment ID, distance, energy, electricity cost, fare revenue, API/compute cost, currency, and source basis; include ordered road-Link energy details under each journey segment.
segment_economics.fare_attribution: Observed whole-trip fare is recorded once on the passenger journey segment; only an explicit per-kilometre fare schedule may allocate revenue to individual road Links.
known_operating_cost_components: EV energy kWh * explicit electricity price per kWh
API/token cost when both measured usage and an explicit token price are available
compute cost when both measured compute usage and an explicit rate are available

segment_types.passenger: use observed segment fare or an explicit fare schedule; if neither exists, fare revenue is null

segment_economics.unknown_value_policy: Keep unknown components null; never treat unknown costs or revenue as zero. If passenger fare revenue or segment electricity cost is unknown, expose the known subtotal but block net-cost route scoring.
segment_economics.route_scoring_gate: The monetary dimension is scoreable only when every segment in the candidate has a known fare revenue amount and a priced electricity cost. For a deadhead segment, revenue is known zero.
segment_economics.profitability_claim: This accounting omits vehicle depreciation, maintenance, insurance, and unpriced taxes/tolls; it does not establish full business profitability.

meeting_transcript_context.transcript_interpretation: The teacher discusses comparing per-distance fare revenue with electricity and token/API expense, and dynamic weights for electricity versus token expense. The recognized 0.6/0.4 and 0.4/0.6 pairs refer to electricity versus token cost in that passage, not explicitly time versus money.
meeting_transcript_context.user_adopted_weight_mapping: For this implementation, the user approved mapping the two pairs to time versus money: (0.6, 0.4) and (0.4, 0.6).
meeting_transcript_context.fare_rate_status: illustrative transcript examples only; do not apply as a frozen tariff or to non-CNY experiments without scenario-specific confirmation

required_inputs.currency: Same explicit currency for all candidates in one decision set.
required_inputs.electricity_price: Explicit nonzero price and source/status are required to score the monetary dimension.
required_inputs.fare_revenue: Observed segment fare or an explicit experiment fare schedule; otherwise report operating-cost-only selection and mark fare unpriced.

outputs: selected candidate and deterministic rank per weight profile
electricity, API/compute cost, fare revenue, net economic cost, currency and source metadata
accounting completeness and excluded business-cost components
